verdicts.reason: Descriptive statement that no registers exist; nothing to verify or exercise.
Quote says overflow/underflow are 1-cycle pulses (checkable every cycle from interface signals); the 'no sticky register' part is descriptive. Check should be assertion only, not both.
Conditional recommendation ('if it should not lose words'); SHOULD is apt, but actor is the software/control owner. Not checkable, so check none is acceptable.

The quote says one write-clock cycle is enough and may be held longer; it is a sequence step for the controller. Strength MUST is acceptable but the actor is the external control owner, not the system.
Step (3) is a requirement on the external control owner, not the system.
Quote states usable-again condition; verifiable by scenario and observable signals.
Quote states read side is always released before write side; checkable from reset-related signals.
Quote states o_sw_rst_busy falls when write side is released.

Restriction applies to software/user (the quote says 'Do not use'), a usage guidance, not a DUT behaviour to check; the claim that busy is 0 for one cycle after fall is a DUT behaviour but is not the core rule.
Quote states words in the FIFO at reset are lost; testable by scenario.

duplicates.reason: All three come from the same quote, but they state different behaviours; merging is not warranted.

questions.question: Does the quote for AF-11.2-02 require holding i_rst_n_sw low for at least one write-clock cycle, or is a shorter pulse tolerated? The text says one cycle is enough, which is not an explicit minimum.
What exactly is 'after the reset has started' in step (3)? Is it detected by o_sw_rst_busy = 1 or by some number of cycles?
